title: thermal-token-econ-scrapbook-a10-l4-a100-h100
body:
Purpose:
Quick, messy working notes tying thermal/power observations to $/token and perf/W for the common inference candidates (A10, L4, A100, H100). Goal: surface knobs for Optimize recommendations (prefer instances that minimize $/token under SLOs, or maximize perf/W when energy constraints matter).

Status: rough lab notes + an early sketch of a tiny cost model. Numbers are experimental — DO NOT SHARE OUTSIDE THE TEAM.

Summary conclusions (high level):
- Under the test profile (short chat / 1.6k context median), A10 appears cheapest on $/million-tokens in these runs, but has lower headroom.
- H100 gives highest absolute throughput and best perf/W in our sample, but its raw $/million-tokens is highest due to sticker hourly cost.
- L4 balances decent tokens/sec and modest cost; it wins on a latency-constrained perf-per-dollar tradeoff for midrange workloads.
- A100 sits between L4 and H100; good raw throughput but lower perf/W in our thermal-limited runs.

Assumptions for the sheet (these are intentionally simplified so we can iterate):
- Benchmark workload: 1.5k context avg, mix of 60% generate / 40% chat-turn echo, batching: auto (continuous batching on runtime), KV cache warm.
- System measured at steady-state 15m window after warmup. Token measurement = model-decoded tokens counted at server boundary.
- Power values are GPU package average as measured by nvidia-smi over the window (not full node power).
- Hourly GPU cost assumptions (on-reservation effective rates used for relative comparisons):
  - A10: $0.60 / hour
  - L4: $1.00 / hour
  - A100: $2.80 / hour
  - H100: $6.50 / hour
(these are blended internal rates + rental equivalents for our cost model; we can swap with real billing once finance gives numbers)

Raw measured datapoints (single-run averages):
- A10:
  - sustained_tokens_per_sec: 1200
  - avg_gpu_power_w: 120
  - tokens_per_sec_per_watt (perf/W): 10
  - tokens_per_hour: 4,320,000
  - $/million_tokens: $0.139

- L4:
  - sustained_tokens_per_sec: 1600
  - avg_gpu_power_w: 140
  - perf/W: ~11.43
  - tokens_per_hour: 5,760,000
  - $/million_tokens: $0.174

- A100:
  - sustained_tokens_per_sec: 2600
  - avg_gpu_power_w: 300
  - perf/W: ~8.67
  - tokens_per_hour: 9,360,000
  - $/million_tokens: $0.299

- H100:
  - sustained_tokens_per_sec: 4200
  - avg_gpu_power_w: 350
  - perf/W: 12
  - tokens_per_hour: 15,120,000
  - $/million_tokens: $0.430

Mini interpretation notes:
- Cheapest $/M token in this run = A10 (~$0.14/M). If your product cares only about minimizing variable token cost for bulk async embedding-like workloads, A10 is attractive.
- If you need peak throughput (reduce cluster size or reduce latency for large fanout), H100 reduces node count significantly (15.12M vs 4.32M tokens/hr), but budget impact is material since $/M is higher.
- Perf/W suggests H100 > L4 > A10 > A100 in this dataset. That is, H100 gives most tokens per watt, which matters if PUE+energy constraints are in scope.

Tradeoff visualization (narrative):
- Plot idea: x-axis = tokens/hr capacity per GPU, y-axis = $/million_tokens. Points: A10 (low x, low y), L4 (mid x, mid y), A100 (higher x, mid-high y), H100 (very high x, high y).
- Another plot: perf/W vs tokens/hr: shows H100 dominates on both axes in our run (best perf/W and highest throughput).

Operational knobs and where Optimize can act:
- Recommendation engine should expose: target SLO (p99 latency), target tokens/hr target or peak capacity, and energy cap (optional).
- If target is strictly minimize $/token with latency unconstrained: recommend A10 or mixed A10 pool for background workloads.
- If target is latency sensitive and throughput required: prefer H100 for headroom, but flag $/token delta and suggest burst-to-H100 policy (baseline L4 or A100, burst H100).
- For mid-range: L4 frequently gives best overall tradeoff (good perf/W, reasonable $/token).

Uncertainties and caveats (things to follow up):
- Node-level power (including CPU, NIC) changes the perf/W rank; we only measured GPU package power. Need full-node energy to estimate datacenter-level perf/W.
- Pricing inputs are rough blended rates. Different procurement or spot/reserved tiers will swing $/M heavily (H100 benefits more from bulk discount).
- Latency SLOs: these throughput slices assume batching is allowed; low-batch low-latency paths will drop tokens/sec and change $/M winners.
- Model variant differences (quantized vs fp16) can change perf/W materially; we tested a single quant level.

Experimental notes / raw commands used:
- runner: perf-bench v2 (internal) with continuous-batch=on, sample-config attached in linked PR.
- power sampling: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw --format=csv -l 1, aggregated and averaged.
- token counting: server-side token counter hook (counts decoded tokens at boundary).

Mini next-steps (actionable):
- [ ] Re-run with full-node power telemetry (DCIM) to compute perf/W at rack scale (responsible: Priya).
- [ ] Replace blended price assumptions with finance-provided reservation and spot curves for us-east-1 (responsible: Miguel).
- [ ] Add low-latency microbenchmark (batch=1) to see cost impact on real-time SLOs.
- [ ] Generate plots for the weekly product review and save as a slide (owner: me).

Notes-to-self: include a second sheet with sensitivity sliders (hourly_price, batch_size, p99_latency_target) and output recommended fleet mix (percent A10/L4/A100/H100). Keep the optimization simple at first: greedy capacity filler until tokens/hr target met (respecting latency tier).

Appendix: quick calculation references used above (copyable):
- tokens_per_hour = sustained_tokens_per_sec * 3600
- $/M_tokens = (hourly_cost / tokens_per_hour) * 1,000,000

End of scrap.

-- SC
